dialogue_history.content: Should “volatile event-driven fast movers” mean the Volatile Event Speculator classification, or also require High Velocity Suspicion Trader? Also, how do you define Order Modification Intensity (OMI)?

“Volatile event-driven fast movers” refers specifically to the Volatile Event Speculator classification, not an additional requirement for High Velocity Suspicion Trader. Order Modification Intensity (OMI) is defined as the order modification frequency divided by (1 minus the cancellation percentage), i.e., modfreq / (1 - cancelpct), with transactions where cancelpct is not less than 1 excluded to avoid division by zero.

For Volatile Event Speculators, should a trader qualify if more than 30% of their transactions have a non-null corporate event, their risk appetite is Aggressive, and at least one transaction has |newsscore − socscore| > 1.0? Then should the average OMI include all eligible transactions of those traders, or only their high-SDF transactions?

Yes—a trader qualifies as a Volatile Event Speculator if more than 30% of their transactions have a non-null corporate event, their risk appetite is Aggressive, and at least one of their transactions has |newsscore − socscore| > 1.0. The average OMI should include all eligible transactions of those qualifying traders, not only their high-SDF transactions.

WITH qualifying_traders AS (
    SELECT t.tradereg
    FROM trader AS t
    JOIN transactionrecord AS r ON r.trdref = t.tradereg
    LEFT JOIN sentimentandfundamentals AS s ON s.transref = r.transreg
    WHERE t.trading_performance #>> '{risklevel,risklevel}' = 'Aggressive'
    GROUP BY t.tradereg
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT r.transreg) FILTER (WHERE s.corpeventprx IS NOT NULL)::numeric
               / COUNT(DISTINCT r.transreg) > 0.30
       AND BOOL_OR(ABS(s.newsscore - s.socscore) > 1.0)

SELECT AVG(r.modfreq / (1 - r.cancelpct)) AS average_omi
FROM transactionrecord AS r
JOIN qualifying_traders AS q ON q.tradereg = r.trdref
WHERE r.cancelpct < 1;
